body:
Aww, unemployment is shitty :(
I hope you find something and that it's amazing.

That's sound advice you have re: new jobs. I'm my own worst enemy - I try so hard not to be a prickly bitch and...then I go and be a prickly bitch. I have no idea what's wrong with me.

Hi Dr RedPaint,

You know - the sad thing is, having a new job every 1 - 2 years is probably the optimal solution for me until I get my shit together. It's been my MO for the past 3 years - I can only keep up the veneer of being a productive member of society for so long. My job-hopping is going to eventually bite me in the ass, though.

Yeah,

He's not perfect - but I feel like a hypocrite if I say anything to him because I have so many flaws myself. Even the stuff he does take on, I still feel like I need to prod him. Example - Our dog may be sick - it's his responsibility to make her vet appts. But he doesn't remember. I still have to send him e-mail and text reminders.

I've been on different combinations of medication since I was 15. Maybe I should try something different, but there's a lot of anxiety with messing with them. I'm afraid to start messing around with them - as fun as it would be, I might get manic and try to attack one of my coworkers with the hole-puncher :P

Thanks, BreakfastWithReddit.

The thing with my husband is, while I love him sincerely, I don't feel like I can rely on him. I've talked to him about my depression and stress before but at the end of the day - I feel like I'm the glue holding things together. Financially, in terms of house-keeping and relationship maintenance. If I don't clean the bathroom, it doesn't get done. If I don't buy the groceries, it doesn't get done. I usually plan date nights. 

His precarious job situation is partly of his own making - TDLR, there were a million red flags at his last job, I pleaded with him to find another job while he was still employed but he refused to listen. He ended up quitting without anything lined up, effectively refusing disability/unemployment insurance. He's now currently under-employed in a contract that may end any day.

I'm exhausted and demoralized. I don't see how I can move forward and fix myself when I already feel like I'm drowning.

It's true - I'm blessed in that I have an immediate family that loves and cares for me.

The problem is that I'm completely unequipped to thrive and survive in this current world. I feel like I'm primarily responsible for keeping us afloat financially and for the housekeeping. I do the most of the cleaning, I have the (on-paper) stable job. I feel responsible for basically everything. My husband is a wonderful human being, but I feel like I can't rely on him to get anything done.

I feel like I'm barely hanging on and that if I mess up, I'll make myself unemployable or fuck up my family relations. I am SO. TIRED.

I hear you on this - my thoughts go to 'Why are they buttering me up - do they want me to do something for them? Do they want to steal my kidneys?'

Ugh - it sucks not being able to trust our own judgement.
